model.relationship: Same inherited model and settings according to run orchestration.
model.limitation: Exact model/runtime settings were not captured; do not infer them from prose or claim exact external reproducibility.

design.wait_repeat: One answer per condition: no skill, prior search skill, initial new Workshop skill, and a separately recorded revised new Workshop skill. The revised run is an iteration, not an independent repeated sample of the same skill contents.
design.health_mapping: One matched-pair smoke test using a documented prompt variant. No baseline or old-skill health comparison.
design.rubric_access: Run procedure instructed agents to receive prompts and applicable skills, not grader rubrics or intended answers. No independent process transcript audit was performed.
design.grading: Post-hoc manual grading against evals/cases.json, by a project agent rather than an independent blinded panel. Scores are diagnostic, not a statistical ranking.
design.compiler: Orchestrator later checked the four native answers with pinned OverPy 9.7.17; accepted flags, diagnostics and element counts are retained verbatim. This report did not rerun compilation.
design.final_content_caveat: After these runs, the maintainer tightened named-API-first/stop-when-supported routing, no-reread guidance, and an OverPy link to waits.md. Those final edits were not re-evaluated.
limitations: One prompt comparison and one related smoke test do not establish statistical superiority or broad correctness.
There are no actual tokenizer measurements or game tests.
Reading-size units are mixed and partly self-reported; byte and character values must not be added as one token count.
The prior skill reported one additional repeated body read and six search-result outputs; headline file-size sums alone understate that condition.
Exact evaluated file snapshots/commits were not captured. Raw records preserve the answers and reported reads, not all reference contents.

It increments only once while I keep holding the button. Make it increment every 0.1 seconds while held, stop on release, and explain why the original behaves that way. Give a complete small native Workshop example.
